Try itModel the AV, step 3: drag slows the AV, more at higher speed
Drag
  • Everything that slows a moving vehicle when no pedal is pressed.
  • Our model gives it as the deceleration it causes, in m/s2.
Rolling resistanceEach tire flattens a little where it meets the road. It slows the AV by 0.15 m/s2 at any speed.
Air dragThe AV pushes the air aside. It slows the AV by \(0.012\,v^2\) m/s2, so twice the speed gives four times the air drag.
AV speed \(v\)try it
AV speed (m/s)Rolling (m/s2)Air (m/s2)Drag, total (m/s2)
40.15\(0.012 \times 4^2 = 0.19\)\(0.15 + 0.19 = 0.34\)
80.15\(0.012 \times 8^2 = 0.77\)\(0.15 + 0.77 = 0.92\)
  • All three steps together: the AV's acceleration \(=\) what the engine delivers \(-\) drag.
  • At 8 m/s, with the most throttle and the lag passed: \(3 - 0.92 = 2.08\) m/s2, so the AV still speeds up.
